markdown_report:
The best first experiment is a **mask-safe recent-history usefulness probe** for the supplied BERT4Rec. At 0% progress, trustworthy diagnostics precede architecture changes. Training-prefix interventions measure fitted-model dependence; useful generalization requires untouched validation targets. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. Training-position margins miss appended-mask inference. Reproduce inference construction and audit target provenance; repeated item IDs alone do not establish leakage.
2. Feedback motivates testing recent-history dependence. Neither sensitivity nor training-prefix ranking establishes usefulness on unseen targets.
3. Missing identity prevents preference assessment. Compatibility, ownership, intent and simulator traits remain unknown without evidence.

**Insights from related work**

1. BERT4Rec supervises selected original positions and appends a mask for inference [1]. Intentional unchanged corruption is valid; shifted-target exposure is not.
2. Counterfactual edits reveal dependence, not causal user effects [2,5]. Perturbations can create unrealistic histories.
3. Sampled metrics can change comparisons [3]. Preserve host selection and acknowledge repeated validation adaptation.

**Directions and framework**

| Direction | Existing measurement | Proposed addition | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inference correctness | Training margins | Mask provenance and padding checks | Correctness does not establish quality |
| History usefulness | No interventions | Paired held-out edits and controls | Training prefixes show dependence only |
| Representation health | Mean cosine | Centered effective rank [4] | Association does not establish causation |

**Three atomic ideas**

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Mask-safe history usefulness probe — 4/7/5.** Originality: combines family-specific controls; interventions are established. Potential: guides training changes; validation reuse limits independence. Difficulty: reuses inference hooks; evaluator access, provenance and positional controls require care.
- **Representation spectrum audit — 3/6/2.** Originality: extends cosine diagnostics; effective rank is established. Potential: detects geometric failures; ranking relevance remains uncertain. Difficulty: sampled SVD is simple; centering and sampling affect estimates.
- **Mixed terminal-mask training — 2/6/4.** Originality: adjusts masking allocation; terminal masking already appears in BERT4Rec. Potential: may improve next-item alignment; may weaken contextual learning. Difficulty: sampling changes are small; budgeted retraining is required.

**Selected algorithm**

First run identity and construction checks. Freeze each retained history before editing, preventing deletion from admitting older events. Compare recent deletion with equally sized older/random deletions and nonpadding recent-window permutation. Include compact-and-repad deletion and position-preserving removal; report their positional-treatment difference. Repeat random controls and count actual tensor edits and no-ops.

Keep model, targets, candidate IDs, eligibility and tie handling fixed. Measure signed target-rank changes, top-10 overlap, standardized target-versus-tenth-negative margins and paired HR@10 differences. Stratify by baseline correctness, history length and edit distance; bootstrap paired users within categories and macro-average equally.

Use deterministic training-prefix holdouts for descriptive dependence only. Assess usefulness on validation only through authorized access reproducing pinned host examples; otherwise report it unavailable. Preserve the evaluator. Intact-history gains support predictive dependence; gains over permutation support order information under that intervention, not causal intent.

Retain diagnostic APIs, definitions and counts; one fixed checkpoint/category, routing, seeds and training limits. Select subsequent changes solely by host macro validation HR@10; reserve final generalization claims for untouched host evaluation.

idea.description: Add a mask-safe recent-history probe to the corrected BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter. Separate fitted-model dependence measured on training prefixes from predictive usefulness measured, when authorized and available, on untouched validation next-item examples. Use controlled inference interventions on exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Current diagnostics measure training-position separation and average embedding alignment, while qualitative feedback raises questions about specific recent interests. Training-prefix perturbations cannot distinguish memorization from generalization. Paired held-out ablations provide stronger evidence of useful history dependence without inventing compatibility, ownership or intent labels.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the trained network through view.model; retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Keep existing family-specific training diagnostics but audit supervision using selected positions, original labels and corruption provenance when available. Input–target equality is not a leakage detector: legitimate repeated items, intentional unchanged corruption and random replacement collisions are possible. If provenance is unavailable, report the audit as unavailable rather than infer leakage. Never use shifted targets exposed through bidirectional input. Training-prefix examples must use only events before their target; a target may legitimately share an ID with an earlier event. Label their results descriptive in-sample dependence, because their events may have contributed to fitting. Validation usefulness requires an authorized source of the pinned validation examples and exact candidates, eligibility, user selection and tie handling. The existing train_loader contract alone does not supply these. Do not infer them, read hidden files or modify the evaluator; report validation intervention metrics unavailable if the host does not expose the required inputs. For training-prefix diagnostics, generate one deterministic set of 99 unique negative real-item IDs per example, excluding its target and prefix items; skip and count examples with insufficient eligible negatives. These candidates do not replace the pinned evaluator. Freeze the already-truncated visible prefix before editing. Use k=min(3,floor(history_length/2)); skip histories shorter than two items. Compare deletion of the final k events, first k events, and 10 uniformly sampled k-subsets without replacement per draw. Permute the last min(5,history_length) nonpadding events with 10 deterministic draws. Record resulting no-ops separately; keep them in primary assigned-intervention effects and report effective-edit sensitivity separately. Compact deletion closes gaps and left-pads again. Position-preserving deletion replaces removed tokens with PAD at their original positions, masks them as keys, and preserves survivor and appended-mask position IDs. This branch requires an explicit position_ids-capable model path; skip it with an availability flag if preserving positions cannot be guaranteed. Both paths must use the same trained network. Append the reserved mask after the retained history, pad to the original maximum length and gather the greatest nonpadding index, never count minus one. Assert tensor construction and event provenance rather than global absence of the target ID. The identity branch must reproduce scores within numerical tolerance in evaluation mode. Freeze candidate eligibility from the baseline even after deletions. Report raw and standardized margins, flagging zero variance; top-10 overlap is intersection size divided by 10. Use average-rank tie handling only for descriptive prefix diagnostics; held-out comparisons must reproduce host tie handling. Use 1,000 paired user bootstrap replicates per category, resampling complete user records with all intervention draws, and form equal-weight macro effects; report percentile 95% intervals as exploratory. Retain baseline-correct/incorrect, history-length and edit-distance strata with counts; these are descriptive, not independent hypothesis tests. Unrestricted permutation can violate temporal availability, so label it an order-corruption stress test and use timestamps to report availability violations when available; an availability-constrained permutation is optional and must be explicitly distinguished. Do not interpret edits as causal user counterfactuals. Keep unavailable metadata categories empty and do not invent ratings, reviews, ownership or simulator traits. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single GPU, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Use local seed-42 random generators so diagnostics do not alter subsequent training RNG state. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts stay beneath the trial directory. No inference architecture change is required. If a later change is introduced, update the embedded predictor writer and checkpoint loading together. All probe execution consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget; cap descriptive prefix diagnostics at 200 deterministically sampled users per category and record counts. Use host macro validation HR@10 for selection, with no test access or independent predictor fusion.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    previous_mode = view.model.training
    initialize local RNG(seed=42)
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        with no_grad():
            metrics = existing_family_specific_training_diagnostics(train_loader)
            audit selected positions, labels and corruption provenance if available
            record unavailable audits explicitly
            sources = [deterministic_training_prefix_examples(max_users=200)]
            if host explicitly provides pinned validation diagnostic inputs:
                sources += [authorized_validation_examples]
            else:
                record validation_usefulness = unavailable
            for source in sources:
                for user, permitted_history, target_event in source:
                    visible = truncate(permitted_history, L-1)  # freeze before edits
                    candidates, eligibility, tie_rule = fixed_protocol(source, visible, target_event)
                    baseline = append_mask_and_left_pad(visible, L)
                    assert provenance excludes target_event and subsequent events
                    branches = identity_and_controlled_edits(visible, local_RNG)
                    for branch in branches:
                        sequence, optional_position_ids = encode_exact_edit_semantics(branch, L)
                        verify mask, padding, surviving events and effective tensor changes
                        features = compatible_log2feats(sequence, optional_position_ids)
                        index = greatest_nonpadding_index(sequence)
                        logits = compatible_predict_score(features[:, index], candidates)
                        apply unchanged eligibility and specified tie handling
                        record rank, HR@10, top10 IDs, raw and standardized margins
                        flag zero variance and unavailable measurements
                    assert identity scores reproduce baseline within tolerance
                    record paired effects, random-draw averages and no-op counts
            aggregate separately by source, category and descriptive strata
            bootstrap complete paired user records within each category, 1000 replicates
            form equal-weight macro effects and exploratory percentile intervals
            attach counts, source labels, uncertainty and metric_definitions
    finally:
        view.model.train(previous_mode)
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, counts, availability and uncertainty
    require evidence-linked findings
    distinguish in-sample dependence, held-out predictive usefulness and causal claims
    treat unavailable identity/compatibility/intent as unknown
    acknowledge validation adaptation, unrealistic edits and budget limits
    never report diagnostic prefix metrics as host validation performance

originality.positive: Combines BERT4Rec supervision provenance, exact inference construction and paired intervention controls in a reproducible adapter.
originality.negative: History perturbations, held-out ablations and paired bootstrap estimates are established; the contribution is primarily methodological integration.

future_potential.positive: Can guide masking, sampling and regularization experiments by separating inference defects, memorized dependence and held-out predictive effects.
future_potential.negative: Utility depends on authorized validation access; repeated validation-guided changes can overfit the small benchmark, and interventions do not establish real user intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing trained checkpoints and compatibility hooks, with no additional model fitting or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact evaluation alignment, corruption provenance, position-preserving deletion and paired uncertainty require additional interfaces and careful checks.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item training and appended-mask next-item inference.
Includes terminal-item masking, reducing the originality of proposing terminal masking alone.
Distinguishes selected supervised positions from corruption choices; the authors' generator supports mixed corruption but defaults to masking every selected position.
limitations: Does not establish this intervention protocol or guarantee useful recency dependence.
Input–target equality alone cannot distinguish valid corruption or repeated interactions from target leakage.

related_work.title: Sequential counterfactual recommendation study
contributions: Investigates history edits that change recommendations, motivating controlled sequence interventions.
limitations: Recommendation changes alone do not establish explanation quality, generalization or causal effects on users.
The paired controls proposed here are a synthesis rather than a reported BERT4Rec protocol.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can alter comparisons between recommendation models.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the pinned host evaluator.
Training-prefix rankings cannot be reported as independent validation results.

related_work.title: ICML 2024 study of embedding collapse
contributions: Motivates measuring concentration in low-dimensional embedding subspaces alongside pairwise cosine similarity.
limitations: Embedding geometry alone does not identify the cause of a BERT4Rec ranking failure.
Effective rank is an auxiliary diagnostic rather than the model-selection objective.

related_work.title: CETD counterfactual explanation study
contributions: Provides additional context for explaining recommendation changes through modified histories.
limitations: Changed recommendations do not independently establish predictive usefulness on unseen targets.
Training-prefix sensitivity cannot resolve memorization versus generalization.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec authors' training-data generator
contributions: Provides implementation evidence for selected-position corruption and retention of original labels.
Supports mixed corruption through mask_prob=0.8 while defaulting to mask_prob=1.0.
limitations: Generator defaults should not be assumed to match the supplied corrected baseline.
Auditing requires actual corruption provenance, not only equality comparisons.

related_work.title: Betello et al. on sequential recommendation robustness
contributions: Reports stronger effects from deleting recent training interactions than early or middle interactions.
Discusses finite rank-biased overlap for ranking comparisons.
limitations: Training-data perturbations differ from fixed-checkpoint inference edits.
Reported robustness effects do not prove that the present model uses recency usefully.

related_work.title: Liu et al. on constrained history shuffling
contributions: Identifies item-availability confounding in unrestricted shuffling and motivates constrained permutations.
limitations: Constraining availability requires trustworthy temporal information.
Even constrained permutations remain predictive ablations rather than causal interventions on user preferences.

related_work.title: Tan et al. on history removal
contributions: Illustrates history removal using padding embeddings, motivating explicit deletion semantics.
limitations: Padding-based removal and compact deletion can change positional behavior differently.
Implementation details must be adapted to the supplied BERT4Rec padding masks and position embeddings.

related_work.title: Le et al. on temporal leakage in recommendation evaluation
contributions: Motivates caution about temporal leakage when interpreting sequential recommendation results.
limitations: Cross-user temporal leakage is distinct from exposing a shifted target to bidirectional attention.
The task requires preserving the supplied splits and pinned evaluator.
